newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldier stabbed at West Bank settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier stabbed at West Bank settlement.

text.p: An Israeli soldier guarding a Jewish settlement was stabbed 20 times and wounded seriously on Tuesday near the West Bank town of Hebron in an apparent Palestinian guerrilla attack, military sources said.
The pre-dawn attack occurred at Omarim settlement south of Hebron. Rescue workers rushed the soldier to a hospital in Beersheba, southern Israel.
A Jewish settler leader was quick to accuse Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat of inciting the attack and demanded a halt to peace moves.

Palestinians are angry at Israeli government decisions to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and to hand over only a third of the West Bank land they had expected in an Israeli troop redeployment due to have taken place last week.

"We found him stabbed all over his body, about 20 stabs mainly in the head, chest and stomach -- penetrating stabs," said paramedic Gadi Abuhatzeira. He described the soldier's condition as "very serious".
Soldiers launched a search for the assailants. Witnesses saw two knives, a mask and a cap at the site.
"What's clear is this incident didn't just happen. Arafat made a threat and also carried it out," Jewish settler leader Ron Schechner told army radio.
"There's no doubt that this is the result of threats and I believe it must be clear on this matter that the government of Israel must not operate under threats," Schechner said.
Israeli military censors barred Reuters from identifying the victim as a soldier for hours pending notification of family.

Near Hebron on Monday, at least 10 Palestinians were injured by Israeli soldiers who used clubs and guns to beat back about 100 Arabs trying to stop workers from opening a road for Jewish settlers, witnesses said.
The clash was the first serious outbreak of Israeli-Arab violence since Arafat spurned an Israeli decision on Friday to hand over another nine percent of the West Bank to Palestinian rule.

Palestinians wanted 30 percent and a say in determining the scope of this and two other pullbacks from mainly rural areas of the West Bank which Israel-PLO interim peace deals mandate must be completed by mid-1998.
